title: RPG Maker for Teens Resource Files

posts.author: technohat
posts.body:
I've got a copy of the book RPG Maker for Teens by Michael Duggan. The book was published in 2012 and the link included in the book to download resource files to go along with the tutorials is no longer valid. Does anybody have the resource files or know where I can get them?
The original link was to
http://www.courseptr.com/downloads
which would redirect to the Cengage Learning center.
Using the Wayback machine eventually gets me to the product page.
https://web.archive.org/web/2012110...ning.com/companions/index.asp?isbn=1435459660
But the Resource Link on that page was not archived.
https://web.archive.org/web/20121105115344/http://www.delmarlearning.com/companions/content/1435459660/Resource_files/index.asp?isbn=1435459660
Since the links to the files are dead and not backed up in the Wayback machine, does anybody have the resource files or know where I can get them?

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
The book has pretty specific info about the author and he worked in a public institution - so unless he's died, it should be pretty possible to get directly in contact with him. That's probably your best bet.
Aside from that...it seems unlikely that whatever the resources were are so special that you can't just use something that comes with the software or is freely available on the forums here.
Even if someone else here had that same book, it's generally not okay to redistribute art someone else made without permission to do so.

posts.author: Avery
posts.body: If there is any describtion or even preview of these resources maybe we can help you track them down or recommend something similar?

If anybody has the book and knows what the files are, even if you no longer have them, please let me know. Thanks!

Are you aware of the differences between versions of RPG Maker? Your profile says you have MZ, and the book is written for VX.
Any typed code or downloaded scripts for VX won't do anything in MZ, they use entirely different programming languages.
Honestly, I suggest you just ditch (or read through without trying to recreate) this book. There are tons of tutorials, including those built into RPG Maker, posts here, the Blog portion of this Web site, and YouTube video series.
It would take you much less time to find materials that are both relevant and immediately usable, and then if there are any design concepts you find useful from reading the book, you can incorporate them.
